long_biography.plain_text:
At seventeen, Hubbard joined KSTP as a prop worker and learned the station through sales, photography, floor direction and production. The business had been founded by his father, Stanley E. Hubbard, giving him an inherited platform but not a ceremonial role. He progressed from station management to the presidency and eventually the top corporate post.

Hubbard's defining personal venture was United States Satellite Broadcasting. Formed in 1981, USSB secured an early direct-broadcast permit and spent years assembling the funding and partnerships needed for service. It began broadcasting alongside DirecTV in 1994, then was acquired by Hughes in a cash-and-stock transaction. That project added a founder-built satellite business to the family broadcasting inheritance and materially expanded his wealth and industry influence.

uncertainties.detail: The exact full-name owner record and family obituary provide an unusually strong person-to-MIMI bridge, and a yacht-owner source separately names Hubbard. The obituary describes use rather than legal title, while no reviewed registry document discloses the beneficial owner. The dossier therefore resolves the person confidently without treating family use or a secondary yacht database as formal title evidence.

The authoritative input and YachtBuyer give Mimi as 39.6 metres and 192 GT, while SuperYacht Times and SuperYachtFan report 244 GT for the same 1977 Burger yacht. Length, builder, year and former-name history converge; the volume discrepancy is preserved as source variance and has no bearing on the biography or wealth classifications.

Stanley Stub or Stanley S. Hubbard, born in 1933, is the subject. His father Stanley Eugene or Stanley E. Hubbard, born in 1897, founded the original broadcasting business and developed its earliest radio and television innovations. Those founder facts are used only to explain the inherited platform and are not attributed to the son.

The dossier uses Inherited and expanded because Hubbard joined and succeeded within a father-founded family company but also expanded its stations, satellite newsgathering and cable interests. His separately founded USSB was a material entrepreneurial achievement. Public sources do not allocate the family-company stake, USSB ownership or Hughes consideration precisely among Hubbard, relatives, trusts and other shareholders.

Hughes filings establish a cash-and-stock acquisition of USSB, while Forbes identifies DirecTV as Hubbard's wealth source. The total company transaction consideration, current Forbes estimate and real-time ranking are not treated as personal cash, retained securities or current net worth.

Forbes's March 2026 profile still identifies Hubbard as chairman and chief executive, and the University of Minnesota calls him the current family patriarch. Other family members run portions of the group. The dossier does not infer detailed voting control, day-to-day workload or succession arrangements from the public title alone.

The 1967 Broadcasting profile and Library of American Broadcasting both give 28 May 1933; the contemporaneous profile also gives St. Paul as birthplace. Forbes's reported age is consistent. These fields are proposed, while no secondary nationality is inferred.
